# ADR 0001 (local) — Where the agents' work becomes visible

Status: accepted, 2026-09-15. Lives in `.local/` because nothing in the repo may say the build is agent-driven.

## Context

Steps are expanded into lanes in `PROGRESS.md`; each lane goes to one crew agent; the main thread ticks boxes
when a report lands and republishes the board artifact. Everything between dispatch and report is invisible:
the user sees "agent running" for twenty minutes and then a report. Which box the agent is on, whether it is
stuck, who did what and how long it took — none of that exists anywhere once the transcript scrolls away.

Three options were on the table:

1. **Amend the artifact** — keep `PROGRESS.md` as the one source of truth, add a log the agents can write, render both as a kanban.
2. **Build a tracker service** — a small API + DB + board, possibly as a demo microservice inside LedgerFlow.
3. **Adopt agent-platform** (`D:/projects/production/ai/agentic-ai/agent-platform`) — it already has a todo
   kanban (`boards → categories → items`, `TodoItem.status`) and a processes screen (`TaskStatus
   pending/running/awaiting_review/completed/failed`, plan as graph/board/timeline/event log).

## Decision

**Option 1.** Two markdown files, one HTML renderer, one stdlib server.

- `PROGRESS.md` stays as it is: main thread only, boxes `- [ ] KEY text` under `### Lane X — Name · mode · who`.
- `.local/log.md` is the agents' side — append only, one line per event:
  `- <UTC ISO> · <agent> · <KEY or lane letter> · start|done|blocked|note · <one line>`.
  Sections `## step NN`; the renderer reads the last one, because box keys repeat from step to step.
  Agents append with one `echo >>` per box; the main thread logs its own inline work as `main` and one
  lane-level line at each dispatch (`· main · R · start · dispatched crew:coder`).
- `.local/progress.html` joins the two on the box key. Status per box:
  ticked → **Done**; last event `done` → **Reported** (the agent says done, the main thread has not accepted —
  agent-platform's `awaiting_review`); `blocked` → red in **Doing**; `start`/`note` → **Doing**; nothing → **To do**.
  Every card carries the agent badge (colour = hash of the name), the time, and start→done duration.
  A lanes strip above the board answers "who is on what right now"; an activity feed on the left is the raw tail.
- Same file, two modes. `python -m http.server 8099 --bind 127.0.0.1` at the repo root → the page polls both
  files every 4 s (the `● live` mark). Published as the artifact → a snapshot as of the last tick
  (`files={"progress.md": "PROGRESS.md", "log.md": ".local/log.md"}`).

Rejected:

- **Option 2** — a second writer. The moment a service owns task state, either the main thread stops editing
  `PROGRESS.md` (and loses the "one file, one editor" rule that keeps four agents from colliding) or the two drift.
  A tracker is also a demo of the wrong thing: LedgerFlow's demo is money, events and measurements, not a todo API.
- **Option 3** — agent-platform runs *its* agents (local models through its own proxy) and its board reflects
  *its* DAG. Claude Code subagents cannot be routed through it; posting into its todo API from here would be a
  copy of the log with none of the join to `PROGRESS.md`. Its status vocabulary was worth stealing; the rest was not.

## What is live now

| what | where | who writes |
|---|---|---|
| step plan, ticks | `PROGRESS.md` | main thread |
| agent events | `.local/log.md` | every lane agent, main for inline work |
| renderer | `.local/progress.html` | — |
| live board | `http://127.0.0.1:8099/.local/progress.html` | `python -m http.server 8099 --bind 127.0.0.1` from the repo root |
| shared snapshot | https://claude.ai/artifact/1BMUASrvJX45WrPFCaxfD5 | republished by the main thread at every tick |
| rules for agents and the main thread | `CLAUDE.local.md` | — |

Operations, in order, for one step: expand lanes in `PROGRESS.md` → `echo "## step NN" >> .local/log.md` →
per lane: log the dispatch line, hand the agent its boxes with the log instruction verbatim → agent logs
`start`/`done`/`blocked` per box → report lands → main thread ticks, republishes → step done → `perf/bench.sh`,
tick under Milestones, expand the next step.

Ceilings, named: the artifact is a snapshot, never live (the hosted page cannot read local files and subagents
have no Artifact tool); concurrent `>>` from three agents to one file is fine at one line per event — if lines
ever interleave, split into `log-<lane>.md`; a box an agent never logs shows as "before log", which is itself the
signal that the prompt lost the instruction.

## Is it a demo for this project?

No, and it should not try to be. What LedgerFlow demonstrates is a saga, an outbox, a read model, a risk model
that cannot reach the ledger, and measured p99s. A kanban of how it was built says "AI wrote this", which is
the one thing the repo must not say; hence `.local/` and `.gitignore`.

Where it *is* reusable: any repo the same crew builds. Copy `.local/progress.html`, the two file conventions
and the CLAUDE.local.md rules; nothing in the renderer is LedgerFlow-specific except the title. If a future
project wants a task tracker as a *product*, agent-platform's todo API is the closer starting point than this —
this is a viewer over markdown, deliberately.

# Build board — contract between the hook, the server and the page

All three live in `.local/` (gitignored). Nothing in the repo may reference them.

## Files (source of truth — the server never owns state)

| file | writer | format |
|---|---|---|
| `PROGRESS.md` | main thread only | milestones + current step expanded into lanes and boxes (see "Plan format") |
| `.local/log.md` | agents (optional), main thread | `- <UTC ISO> · <agent label> · <KEY or lane letter> · start\|done\|blocked\|note · <one line>` under `## step NN` headings |
| `.local/events.jsonl` | `.local/hooks/emit.py` (Claude Code hooks, every session in this project) | one JSON object per line, schema below |

## Plan format (`PROGRESS.md`)

```
**Status (2026-09-15):** 16 / 32 steps done · milestone 2 of 7 closed · step 16 in progress (26 / 33 boxes).
## Milestones
### M1 — Name ✅
- [x] 01 Step title
- [ ] 16 Step title — **current**
## Current step: 16 — Title
Done when: …(one paragraph)…
Decisions taken before the lanes (keep consistent):
- …
### Lane R — risk-service · parallel · one agent
_touches: `services/risk-service/**`, `pom.xml`_
- [x] R1 box text (markdown inline: `code`, **bold**)
- [ ] R2 box text
## Next up
```
Lane heading parts after `·` are tags; one of them is a mode word: `serial | parallel | inline | optional`.
Box keys are `<lane letter><n>`. Keys repeat from step to step — only the last `## step NN` section of `log.md`
and only events with `step == current` are joined to the current plan.

## Event schema (`events.jsonl`)

Common: `ts` (UTC ISO ms, `Z`), `session` (8-char session id), `agent` (17-char agent id, or `main`),
`type` (agent type e.g. `crew:coder`, or `main`), `step` (int, current step at the time), `ev`.

| `ev` | extra fields |
|---|---|
| `agent.start` | `lane` (letter, if the prompt began with `Lane X`), `title` (text after `Lane X —`) |
| `agent.stop` | — |
| `tool.pre` | `tool`, `id` (tool_use_id); Bash: `cmd` (≤400 chars), `desc`; Edit/Write/Read: `file` (repo-relative); Grep/Glob: `pattern`, `file`; Agent (a dispatch from the main thread): `desc`, `subagent`, `lane`, `title` |
| `tool.post` | `tool`, `id`, `ms` (duration); Bash: `out`, `err` (last 600 chars each), `interrupted`; Edit/Write: `out` may be absent |

Attribution rules the page applies:
- agent → lane: `agent.start.lane`; if missing, the nearest earlier `tool.pre` with `tool == "Agent"` from the same session whose `lane` is set and not yet claimed; else `?`.
- `agent == "main"` rows are the main thread (lane `C` when the current step has a Lane C, else `main`).
- tool event → box: the `log.md` `start` line for a KEY by the same agent label opens a window that closes at that agent's next `start`/`done` line; tool events by that agent inside the window belong to the box. (Agent label in `log.md` is self-reported, e.g. `crew:coder`; match on `type` when the label equals a type, otherwise leave unattributed.)
- box status: ticked in `PROGRESS.md` → **done**; last log line `done` → **reported**; `blocked` → **blocked**; `start`/`note` → **doing**; else **todo**.
- agent live: `agent.start` seen, no `agent.stop` from the same agent id, and last event < 30 min ago.

## Server (`.local/board.py`) — Python 3 stdlib only, `ThreadingHTTPServer`, binds `127.0.0.1`, port arg default 8099

| route | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `GET /`, `GET /.local/progress.html` | the page, `text/html; charset=utf-8`, `Cache-Control: no-store` |
| `GET /api/state` | `{"progress": md, "log": md, "events": [last 5000 objects], "now": iso}` |
| `GET /api/stream` | SSE. Poll the three files every 250 ms (mtime+size); on change send `event: progress` / `event: log` (data = JSON string of the whole file) or `event: events` (data = JSON array of the new lines only, tailed by byte offset). `event: ping` every 15 s. Handle client disconnect (`BrokenPipeError`, `ConnectionAbortedError`, `ConnectionResetError`) by returning. |
| `POST /api/log` | JSON `{"agent","key","status","note"}` → append `- <UTC now> · agent · key · status · note` to `.local/log.md`; or `text/plain` body = the line verbatim (prefixed with `- ` if missing). 204. |
| `GET /progress.md`, `/log.md`, `/events.jsonl` | raw files, `no-store` (same names the artifact snapshot uses) |

Silence the per-request access log. Ignore a malformed JSONL line rather than dying. Run: `python .local/board.py` from the repo root.

## Page (`.local/progress.html`)

Two modes, same file: `location.protocol === "http:"` → `/api/state` then `EventSource("/api/stream")`, live dot on;
otherwise (published artifact) → `fetch("progress.md")`, `fetch("log.md")`, `fetch("events.jsonl")` once, snapshot.
Head: `<meta charset="utf-8">` first line, then `<title>`; no `<html>/<head>/<body>` tags (the artifact host wraps it).
Only script allowed from a CDN: `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/marked/4.3.0/marked.min.js`. Everything else inline.

# ADR 0001 (local) — Where the agents' work becomes visible

Status: accepted 2026-09-15, revised the same day (v2: hooks + SSE replaced hand-written log lines + polling).
Lives in `.local/` because nothing in the repo may say the build is agent-driven.

## Context

Steps are expanded into lanes in `PROGRESS.md`; each lane goes to one crew agent; the main thread ticks boxes when a
report lands and republishes the board artifact. Everything between dispatch and report was invisible: "agent running"
for twenty minutes, then a report. Which box the agent is on, what it is running, whether it is stuck, who did what and
how long it took — none of that existed once the transcript scrolled away.

Options on the table:

1. **Amend the artifact** — `PROGRESS.md` stays the plan; agents write a log line per box; render both as a kanban. (v1, shipped first.)
2. **Own tracker service** — API + DB + board, possibly as a demo microservice inside LedgerFlow.
3. **Adopt agent-platform** (`D:/projects/production/ai/agentic-ai/agent-platform`) — has a todo kanban and a
   processes screen (`TaskStatus pending/running/awaiting_review/completed/failed`, plan as graph/board/timeline/event log).

v1 answered "who is on what" only as well as the agents remembered to `echo` a line. The user's requirement after
seeing it: live, reactive to the agents' real actions and outputs, tagged with the agent's id, with commands visible —
and DX first, i.e. no discipline the agents can forget.

## Decision (v2)

**The harness reports, not the agents.** Claude Code hooks are the source of every event; a stdlib server pushes them
to the page over SSE; markdown stays the plan.

Probed, not assumed (2026-09-15, Claude Code 2.1.238, desktop app): hooks in `.claude/settings.local.json` hot-reload
without a restart; `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` fire inside subagents and carry `agent_id` + `agent_type`;
`SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` carry the id and (at stop) the transcript path; the subagent transcript's first line — the
prompt — is on disk ~90 ms before `SubagentStart` fires; `PostToolUse` for Bash carries `stdout`/`stderr`/`interrupted`
and `duration_ms`. Project-level hooks fire for **every** session in the project, so a second session's agents show
up on the same board. `.claude/settings.local.json` is covered by the user's global gitignore — nothing to hide in the repo.

Pieces (all in `.local/`, contract in `.local/board-spec.md`):

| piece | file | role |
|---|---|---|
| plan | `PROGRESS.md` | milestones → steps (stories) → lanes → boxes (tasks). Main thread only. |
| emitter | `.local/hooks/emit.py` | hook → one JSON line in `.local/events.jsonl`: `agent.start` (lane parsed from a prompt that begins `Lane X —`), `agent.stop`, `tool.pre` (cmd / file / pattern), `tool.post` (ms, stdout/stderr tail, interrupted). Never fails the tool call. |
| log | `.local/log.md` | optional box-level lines from agents (`start` / `done` / `blocked` / `note`); still the only way to say "R3 is done" before the main thread ticks. |
| server | `.local/board.py` | `ThreadingHTTPServer` on 127.0.0.1:8099. `/api/state`, `/api/stream` (SSE, 250 ms file poll), `POST /api/log`, raw files. Stateless: files are the truth. |
| page | `.local/progress.html` | Stories rail · Board (To do / Doing / Reported / Done) · Agents (swimlane timeline, one row per agent id, ticks per tool, live edge) · Activity (tail with stdout/stderr) · detail panel. Same file published as the artifact = snapshot. |

Statuses (borrowed from agent-platform's `TaskStatus`): **todo** → **doing** (agent live on the lane or a `start` line)
→ **reported** (agent said `done`, main thread has not ticked — its `awaiting_review`) → **done** (ticked); **blocked** in red.

Rejected:

- **Option 2 as a service with its own state** — a second writer. The moment a service owns task state, either the
  main thread stops editing `PROGRESS.md` (losing the one-file-one-editor rule that keeps four agents from colliding)
  or the two drift. The server here owns nothing; kill it and nothing is lost.
- **Option 3** — agent-platform runs *its* agents through *its* proxy and its board reflects *its* DAG. Claude Code
  subagents cannot be routed through it; posting into its todo API would be a copy of the events with none of the
  join to the plan. Its status vocabulary was worth taking; the rest was not.
- **Polling the files from the page (v1)** — 4 s latency and a full re-render per poll. SSE is one stdlib handler.
- **Agents narrating their own progress (v1)** — the log line was the thing they forgot. Kept as optional refinement
  for box-level state; the tool stream needs nothing from them.

## Operations

```
python .local/board.py            # from the repo root; http://127.0.0.1:8099 — open it in the Browser pane
```
Per step: expand lanes in `PROGRESS.md` → `echo "## step NN" >> .local/log.md` → dispatch each lane with a prompt that
begins `Lane X — <name>` (that is how the emitter names the lane) → watch → report lands → tick, republish
(`Artifact(... files={"progress.md": "PROGRESS.md", "log.md": ".local/log.md", "events.jsonl": ".local/events.jsonl"})`).
Agents that want box-level state: `curl -s -XPOST localhost:8099/api/log -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"agent":"crew:coder","key":"R3","status":"done","note":"tests green"}'` or the `echo >> .local/log.md` line.

## Ceilings, named

- The artifact is a snapshot per republish, never live: the hosted page cannot reach the local server.
- `events.jsonl` grows ~1 line per tool call (a busy step is a few thousand lines, a few MB). The page loads the last
  5000; rotate the file at a step boundary if the publish payload gets heavy.
- Lane attribution needs the prompt to start with `Lane X`; anything else shows as `?` — honest, and the signal that a
  dispatch went out without the convention.
- Two hook subprocesses per Bash/Edit/Write call (~40 ms each, Python startup). Read/Grep/Glob take one. Noticeable
  only on Read-heavy agents; acceptable.
- Tool output is clipped to the last 600 chars per event; the transcript has the rest.

## Is it a demo for this project?

No, and it should not try to be. LedgerFlow demonstrates a saga, an outbox, a read model, a risk model that cannot
reach the ledger, and measured p99s. A board of how it was built says "AI wrote this" — the one thing the repo must not
say; hence `.local/` and `.gitignore`.

Reusable as-is for any repo the same crew builds: copy `.local/{hooks,board.py,progress.html,board-spec.md}`, the
hooks block of `.claude/settings.local.json`, and the `PROGRESS.md` conventions; only the page title is project-specific.
A tracker as a *product* would start from agent-platform's todo API, not from this — this is a viewer over files, by design.

(`marked.parseInline` on escaped input, for task text / touches / decisions only). Fonts from Google Fonts (IBM Plex
Sans + Mono) with a real fallback stack. Everything else inline.

---
name: ledgerflow-board
description: The local build board (hooks → events.jsonl → board.py on 8099 → progress.html/artifact) and the text API the main thread should read instead of the files
metadata:
  type: project
---

Built 2026-09-15. Everything in `.local/` (gitignored) + hooks in `.claude/settings.local.json` (globally gitignored).
Contract: `.local/board-spec.md`; decisions + ceilings: `.local/adr/0001-agent-board.md`.

- `.local/hooks/emit.py` — Claude Code hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, SubagentStart/Stop) → one JSON
  line per event in `.local/events.jsonl` with agent id, type, lane (parsed from a prompt that **begins** `Lane X — …`),
  cmd/file, ms, stdout/stderr tail, failed. Fires for every session in the project. Hooks hot-reload, no restart.
- `.local/board.py` — stdlib server, `python .local/board.py` from the repo root (127.0.0.1:8099). Parses `PROGRESS.md`
  (nested tasks by 2-space indent, `## Sandbox:` stories), pools `.local/log.md`, joins events, tails transcripts for
  model + tokens, writes `.local/model.json`, SSE `/api/stream`.
- Text APIs for Claude (read these, not the files): `/api/summary`, `/api/next`, `/api/wip`, `/api/lane/X`,
  `/api/task/KEY`, `/api/agent/<id suffix>`, `?format=json`; `POST /api/tick {"key","done"}` (main thread only),
  `POST /api/log {"agent","key","status","note"}`.
- Page `.local/progress.html` = renderer of the model (Stories rail · Board · Agents timeline · Activity · sidebar).
  Artifact https://claude.ai/artifact/1BMUASrvJX45WrPFCaxfD5 is a snapshot: publish with
  `files={"model.json": ".local/model.json", "events.jsonl": {"from": ".local/events.jsonl", "contentType": "text/plain"}}`.

**Why:** the user could not see what agents were doing; v1 (agents echo log lines) was forgotten by the agents, so the
harness reports instead. Not a LedgerFlow demo — the repo must not say it was agent-built.
**How to apply:** start the server at session start if `curl -s localhost:8099/api/summary` fails; lane prompts start
with `Lane X — name`; read the API before reading `PROGRESS.md`. See [[ledgerflow-progress]], [[ledgerflow-rebuild-decisions]].
